quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the train has passed.
No, never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. Warning signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Speed up to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a cyclist, slow down and leave plenty of space. Cyclists have less protection than car drivers. Passing too fast can force a cyclist off course.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as what sign?

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop and yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: Why is space between your vehicle and others important?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected events.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected events.
questions.explanation: Leaving plenty of space around your vehicle gives you enough time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the vehicle ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When signals warn of an approaching train, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered gates or a train whistle.

questions.question: You find a defect that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slower.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe driving right away. Fix problems before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: Using your turn signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Is only needed if other cars are nearby.
Is good practice and required by law.
Is only needed during the move, not before.
Is not needed for slow maneuvers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is good practice and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Signal before pulling away from a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What do downward-pointing triangular signs mean?

options.text: School zone ahead.
Yield to other traffic.
Construction zone ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-pointing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. You may proceed when the road is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield.
Drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action shown is forbidden. These signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down entering, speed up leaving.
Keep the same speed through the curve.
Speed up entering, slow down leaving.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down entering, speed up leaving.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and gradually increase speed as you exit. Speeding into a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It makes alcohol less dangerous.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs can slow your brain and make driving unsafe. When you mix drugs with alcohol, the crash risk is much higher.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral right away. Press the brake pedal with steady pressure. When it is safe, pull to the side of the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: A coming intersection.
Road construction.
A curve ahead in the road.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve ahead in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road will curve to the right ahead.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangle sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down and let other cars and pedestrians go first. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.
Move to the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right side of the road and stop. Let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in an intersection, go through it first, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
A special speed zone.
A road with limits on stereo volume.
A television show.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, back, and front. Cars in these spots cannot be seen. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Your power steering stops working. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer hard, slow down, drive to a safe place, and stop.
Slam on the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer hard, slow down, drive to a safe place, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, steering will be harder. Slow down and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: It starts raining while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When it rains hard and you cannot see well, slow down. Turn on your headlights. If rain is very heavy, pull over and stop until it clears.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Drive with the flow of traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: When can you carefully drive through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection as it turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection as it turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you can carefully continue through.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted across traffic lanes?

options.text: On curves and on hills.
Next to churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway on-ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show drivers exactly where to stop.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you a false sense of confidence.
It hurts your thinking ability.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, hurts your coordination, and makes it hard to judge distance and react to what is around you.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always stop completely at a stop sign before entering the intersection. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop right away and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that work is being done on or near the road. Drive with extra care when you see these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when you see other drivers acting angry?

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Keep away from the situation.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Stay away from angry drivers. Avoid looking at them or making gestures that might upset them. Slow down, move away, or do whatever you can safely do to stay out of danger.

questions.question: What should you do if you get stuck in a snowstorm?

options.text: Get out of the car and look for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are more likely to be found.
questions.explanation: If you get stuck in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers will find you more easily if you stay in your vehicle. It is also unsafe to walk around in a snowstorm.

questions.question: What should you do when passing a car that just parked on the side of the road?

options.text: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Expect the driver to wait until you pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the car door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, be ready for the driver to open the door. Drive with caution near parked vehicles.

questions.question: You are waiting in line at a stop sign. Cars ahead have gone through with no cross traffic. Can you go without stopping again?

options.text: Yes, you can go without stopping again.
No, you must stop completely at the stop sign or stop line.
Yes, you can slowly roll past the stop sign.
Yes, you can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you must stop completely at the stop sign or stop line.
questions.explanation: You must always stop completely at a stop sign and check for traffic before going. Don't skip this step just because other cars went through.

questions.question: When must you yield to a transit bus that is entering traffic?

options.text: Only if there are cars behind you.
If the bus has its hazard lights on.
When the bus has its turn signal on and a flashing "Yield" sign is lit.
Never. The bus must wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the bus has its turn signal on and a flashing "Yield" sign is lit.
questions.explanation: Yield to a transit bus when it signals to enter traffic and has a flashing "Yield" sign. Slow down or move over to let the bus safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the side of the road with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane road and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, cars going both directions must stop and stay stopped as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes road conditions less than perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes road conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any other condition is not safe. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the speed limit.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If safe, change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If safe, change lanes to avoid driving next to the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes if possible to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as you can. Always slow down and be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot continue driving in your current direction.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less well.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
As you slow down, the road becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less well.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less effectively your tires remove water. If you go too fast, your tires lose grip and you hydroplane—you slide on a layer of water on the road.
